name: 序列帧动画
description: 制作连续动作序列帧，切帧并合成 GIF 动画。
instructions:
## Purpose
Create short sprite animations with continuous, intentional motion around a shared anchor, not a collection of unrelated poses. Reply in the user's language.

## Inputs
Reuse this session's character reference images. Determine the action, frame count, grid, playback FPS and loop requirement. Default to a simple 8-frame loop (4 columns, 2 rows), 8 FPS. Choose in-place motion unless the user requests travel. If the user supplies separate frames, use their explicit order and skip generation and splitting. Clarify ambiguous versions, do not request re-upload of existing images.

## Outputs
A GIF animation, ordered PNG frames and an in-app playback preview. No video or audio. GIF has limited colors and binary transparency; retain PNG frames for fidelity.

## Steps
Before generation, define one coordinate system for every equal-size cell: top-left origin, x rightward, y downward. Use normalized cell coordinates because generated pixel dimensions are not guaranteed. Choose a fixed canvas anchor and explain its meaning: for a standing character, default to the neutral stance's ground-projected root at (0.5, 0.85). This is an invisible registration point, not a body part that must stay still or a point to draw. For floating or traveling actions choose an appropriate origin and explicit root trajectory.
Plan each frame's action phase and intended root offset (dx, dy) from that anchor. Keep the frame origin, camera and drawing scale fixed. Preserve identity, proportions, lighting and background. Allow planned body bounce, squash/stretch, head movement and foot lifts relative to the anchor; do not freeze the head, torso and feet together. Reserve the same safe area across all cells for the full motion, including raised hands. Never independently center, crop or resize a pose to fill its cell. For loops plan a seamless last-to-first transition without a duplicated endpoint.
Generate ONE equal-cell grid sheet with create_images, output_mode=compose, count=1 and relevant references. Put the coordinate convention, numeric anchor, per-frame offsets/action phases, consistent scale and safe area into the actual image prompt. Ask for row-major frames, no gaps, borders, labels, visible anchor marks or overlap between cells. Generation is approximate, not a guarantee of exact grid geometry, anchor placement or motion consistency.
Use view_image to inspect the sheet against the planned anchor and trajectory. Distinguish unintended registration drift from intentional movement; do not infer alignment from each pose's bounding-box center or lowest visible pixel. If there is visible drift, changing scale, clipping or incorrect grid geometry, explain the defect and ask before paid regeneration. Do not guess crop parameters or promise automatic alignment.
Call split_sprite_sheet with the image ID, exact rows, columns, frame_count and margin/spacing (default zero). Keep full equal-size cells and their original coordinates. Use the returned ordered frameFiles with compose_animation, fps and looped. Neither tool realigns characters. If the grid cannot be divided evenly, stop and explain instead of repeatedly guessing. Tools enforce their own size/frame limits.

## Acceptance
Offer animation playback and PNG frame export for user inspection. Check shared frame dimensions, anchor-relative placement, planned root trajectory, scale, clipping, identity and loop endpoints. Inspect relevant returned frames with view_image if the sheet leaves a specific issue unclear, within tool limits. State that encoded success alone does not verify smoothness or seamless looping. Report visible defects and let the user judge actual motion. Never claim to have watched the animation from only a still image.

## Limits
No automatic interpolation, background removal, character alignment or video generation. Prompt constraints reduce drift but cannot guarantee it is absent. Do not remove intended motion through per-frame recentering or foot/bounding-box alignment. Additional paid regeneration requires user approval. Keep originals and completed results. Local cutting/encoding does not consume the image-generation count budget.
